claim: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) signaling is a ubiquitous post-translational modification that acts as a cellular nutrient sensor.
source: O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) signaling, a ubiquitous post-translational modification that acts as a cellular nutrient sensor, can significantly enhance in vivo neuron regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract describing O-GlcNAc signaling's known function.

claim: Modulation of O-GlcNAc signaling can significantly enhance in vivo neuron regeneration.
source: Previously, we have shown that modulation of O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) signaling, a ubiquitous post-translational modification that acts as a cellular nutrient sensor, can significantly enhance in vivo neuron regeneration.
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors (Taub et al., 2018) and is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Glycolysis is essential for ogt-1 loss of function mediated increased regenerative outgrowth.
source: Performing in vivo laser axotomy and measuring subsequent regeneration of individual neurons in C. elegans, we find that glycolysis, serine synthesis pathway (SSP), one-carbon metabolism (OCM), and the downstream transsulfuration metabolic pathway (TSP) are all essential in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The serine synthesis pathway (SSP) is essential for ogt-1 loss of function mediated increased regenerative outgrowth.
source: Performing in vivo laser axotomy and measuring subsequent regeneration of individual neurons in C. elegans, we find that glycolysis, serine synthesis pathway (SSP), one-carbon metabolism (OCM), and the downstream transsulfuration metabolic pathway (TSP) are all essential in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: One-carbon metabolism (OCM) is essential for ogt-1 loss of function mediated increased regenerative outgrowth.
source: Performing in vivo laser axotomy and measuring subsequent regeneration of individual neurons in C. elegans, we find that glycolysis, serine synthesis pathway (SSP), one-carbon metabolism (OCM), and the downstream transsulfuration metabolic pathway (TSP) are all essential in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The transsulfuration metabolic pathway (TSP) is essential for ogt-1 loss of function mediated increased regenerative outgrowth.
source: Performing in vivo laser axotomy and measuring subsequent regeneration of individual neurons in C. elegans, we find that glycolysis, serine synthesis pathway (SSP), one-carbon metabolism (OCM), and the downstream transsulfuration metabolic pathway (TSP) are all essential in this process.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: The regenerative effects of ogt-1 mutation are abrogated by genetic and/or pharmacological disruption of OCM.
source: The regenerative effects of ogt-1 mutation are abrogated by genetic and/or pharmacological disruption of OCM and the SSP linking OCM to glycolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using genetic mutations and pharmacological treatments described in the manuscript.

claim: The regenerative effects of ogt-1 mutation are abrogated by genetic and/or pharmacological disruption of the SSP linking OCM to glycolysis.
source: The regenerative effects of ogt-1 mutation are abrogated by genetic and/or pharmacological disruption of OCM and the SSP linking OCM to glycolysis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using genetic mutations and pharmacological treatments described in the manuscript.

claim: Enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 mutants is dependent only on the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway.
source: Testing downstream branches of this pathway, we find that enhanced regeneration is dependent only on the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data testing different branches of the metabolic pathway.

claim: RNA sequencing reveals dramatic transcriptional changes by the ogt-1 mutation in genes involved in glycolysis, OCM, TSP, and ATP metabolism.
source: These results are further supported by RNA sequencing that reveals dramatic transcriptional changes by the ogt-1 mutation, in the genes involved in glycolysis, OCM, TSP, and ATP metabolism.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The beneficial effects of the ogt-1 mutation can be recapitulated by metabolic supplementation of the OCM metabolite methionine in wild-type animals.
source: Strikingly, the beneficial effects of the ogt-1 mutation can be recapitulated by simple metabolic supplementation of the OCM metabolite methionine in wild-type animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing methionine supplementation effects on regeneration.

claim: Cellular metabolism plays an essential role in the regrowth and regeneration of a neuron following physical injury.
source: Cellular metabolism plays an essential role in the regrowth and regeneration of a neuron following physical injury.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction, drawing from general scientific understanding.

claim: The importance of metabolic pathways in neuronal regeneration including the insulin-signaling pathway, energy metabolism, and mitochondrial function have been reported by several groups.
source: The importance of metabolic pathways, particularly in neuronal regeneration including the insulin-signaling pathway, energy metabolism, and mitochondrial function have been reported in research articles by several groups (Byrne et al., 2014; Cartoni et al., 2016; Han et al., 2016; Han et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple research articles.

claim: Perturbation in O-GlcNAc signaling substantially increased axonal regeneration in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: In a previous study our group demonstrated that perturbation in O-GlcNAc signaling, a post-translational modification of serine and threonine that is known to act as a nutrient sensor, substantially increased axonal regeneration in Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: A reduction of O-GlcNAc levels, due to deletion mutation of the ogt-1, induces the AKT-1 branch of the insulin-signaling pathway to utilize glycolysis and significantly enhanced neuronal regeneration.
source: Carrying out in vivo laser axotomies, we demonstrated that a reduction of O-GlcNAc levels, due to deletion mutation of the ogt-1, induces the AKT-1 branch of the insulin-signaling pathway to utilize glycolysis and significantly enhanced neuronal regeneration.
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors (Taub et al., 2018) and is supported by citation.

claim: Inhibition of the glycolytic pathway through RNAi knockdown of phosphoglycerate kinase (pgk-1) or loss of function of phosphofructokinase-1.1 (pfk-1.1) specifically suppressed ogt-1 enhanced regeneration but did not alter wild-type regeneration.
source: Inhibition of the glycolytic pathway through RNAi knockdown of phosphoglycerate kinase (pgk-1) or loss of function of phosphofructokinase-1.1 (pfk-1.1) specifically suppressed ogt-1 enhanced regeneration but did not alter wild-type regeneration (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: Supplementation with glucose in wild-type animals is sufficient to increase axonal regeneration after axotomy.
source: Furthermore, supplementation with glucose in wild-type animals is sufficient to increase axonal regeneration after axotomy (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: Increased glycolysis averts metabolic flux toward OCM to regulate numerous biological processes including molecular reprogramming, immunological functions as well as neuronal development and function.
source: Numerous reports suggest that increased glycolysis averts metabolic flux toward OCMto regulate numerous biological processes including molecular reprogramming, immunological functions as well as neuronal development and function (Iskandar et al., 2010; Konno et al., 2017; Yu et al., 2019b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple research articles.

claim: Studies have reported the importance of metabolic amendments of OCM, the SSP and the TSP in neuronal development, structure, function, and regeneration.
source: In addition, studies have reported the importance of metabolic amendments of OCM, the SSP and the TSP in neuronal development, structure, function, and regeneration (Iskandar et al., 2010; Bonvento and Bolaños, 2021; Lam et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple research articles.

claim: Both functional OCM and glycolytic flux towards OCM via the SSP are essential for enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals.
source: Measuring neuronal regeneration in C. elegans following laser axotomy under genetic and pharmacological perturbations of metabolic pathways, we demonstrate that both functional OCM and glycolytic flux towards OCM via the SSP are essential for enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments with genetic and pharmacological manipulations.

claim: Metabolic pathways from OCM through the TSP, that result in cystathionine metabolism into Acetyl-CoA via the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway, is critical for enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals.
source: From there, we observed that metabolic pathways from OCM through the TSP, that result in cystathionine metabolism into Acetyl-CoA via the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway, is also critical.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data testing different metabolic pathways.

claim: ogt-1 (deletion, ok1474 strain crossed with zdis-5) mutation increases neuronal regeneration following laser axotomy of mechanosensory neurons in C. elegans.
source: Performing laser axotomy on individual neurons in vivo and measuring regenerative outgrowth after 24 hr, we found that either ogt-1 (deletion, ok1474 strain crossed with zdis-5) mutation or the enzymatically ogt-1 dead allele (ogt-1-dAl; OG1135 strain crossed with zdis-5) equally increase neuronal regeneration following laser axotomy of mechanosensory neurons in C. elegans (Figure 1A–B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: The enzymatically ogt-1 dead allele (ogt-1-dAl; OG1135 strain crossed with zdis-5) increases neuronal regeneration following laser axotomy of mechanosensory neurons in C. elegans.
source: Performing laser axotomy on individual neurons in vivo and measuring regenerative outgrowth after 24 hr, we found that either ogt-1 (deletion, ok1474 strain crossed with zdis-5) mutation or the enzymatically ogt-1 dead allele (ogt-1-dAl; OG1135 strain crossed with zdis-5) equally increase neuronal regeneration following laser axotomy of mechanosensory neurons in C. elegans (Figure 1A–B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from laser axotomy experiments shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Reduced O-GlcNAc levels due to the loss of function of ogt-1 will effectively block the metabolic flux into the HBP, diverting metabolites towards glycolysis.
source: Reduced O-GlcNAc levels due to the loss of function of ogt-1 will effectively block the metabolic flux into the HBP, diverting metabolites towards glycolysis (Yi et al., 2012; Jóźwiak and Forma, 2014; Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles describing the metabolic effects of ogt-1 loss of function.

claim: gfat-1 and gfat-2 are orthologs of the human glutamine-fructose-6-phosphate transaminase 1 (GFPT1).
source: gfat-1 and gfat-2, orthologs of the human glutamine-fructose-6-phosphate transaminase 1 (GFPT1), catalyzes the very first and rate limiting step of HBP (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gene orthology.

claim: gfat-1 and gfat-2 catalyze the very first and rate limiting step of HBP.
source: gfat-1 and gfat-2, orthologs of the human glutamine-fructose-6-phosphate transaminase 1 (GFPT1), catalyzes the very first and rate limiting step of HBP (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the enzymatic function of these genes.

claim: Knocking down either gfat-1 or gfat-2 in the wild type worms significantly increases the regeneration of mechanosensory neurons, similar to ogt-1 loss of function.
source: We found that knocking down either gfat-1 or gfat-2 in the wild type worms, significantly increase the regeneration of mechanosensory neurons, similar to ogt-1 loss of function, (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: C. elegans has two orthologs of mammalian PK, pyk-1 and pyk-2.
source: C. elegans has two orthologs of mammalian PK, pyk-1 and pyk-2, with pyk-1 expression primarily in neurons including the mechanosensory neurons ALM and PLM and pyk-2 showing limited neuronal expression (Hammarlund et al., 2018; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hammarlund et al., 2018 and expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and 1B.

claim: pyk-1 expression is primarily in neurons including the mechanosensory neurons ALM and PLM.
source: C. elegans has two orthologs of mammalian PK, pyk-1 and pyk-2, with pyk-1 expression primarily in neurons including the mechanosensory neurons ALM and PLM and pyk-2 showing limited neuronal expression (Hammarlund et al., 2018; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hammarlund et al., 2018 and expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: pyk-2 shows limited neuronal expression.
source: C. elegans has two orthologs of mammalian PK, pyk-1 and pyk-2, with pyk-1 expression primarily in neurons including the mechanosensory neurons ALM and PLM and pyk-2 showing limited neuronal expression (Hammarlund et al., 2018; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hammarlund et al., 2018 and expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The knock down of pyk-1, via neuron-specific RNAi, does not affect the enhanced regeneration in the ogt-1 mutant.
source: Interestingly, we found that the knock down of pyk-1, via neuron-specific RNAi, does not affect the enhanced regeneration in the ogt-1 mutant but significantly increases regeneration in WT (Figure 1A and D, Figure 1—source data 1), to levels similar to that of ogt-1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The knock down of pyk-1, via neuron-specific RNAi, significantly increases regeneration in WT to levels similar to that of ogt-1.
source: Interestingly, we found that the knock down of pyk-1, via neuron-specific RNAi, does not affect the enhanced regeneration in the ogt-1 mutant but significantly increases regeneration in WT (Figure 1A and D, Figure 1—source data 1), to levels similar to that of ogt-1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Overall pyk-1 activity is significantly down in ogt-1 worms.
source: Furthermore, performing pyk-1 activity assay in whole worm lysate we observed that over all pyk-1 activity is significantly down in ogt-1 worms (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pyk-1 activity assays shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The final step of glycolysis, mediated by PYK-1, is not involved in the enhanced regeneration of the ogt-1 animals.
source: These results suggest the final step of glycolysis, mediated by PYK-1, is not in fact involved in the enhanced regeneration of the ogt-1 animals.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing pyk-1 knockdown does not affect ogt-1 regeneration.

claim: atp-3 is an ortholog of human ATP5PO (ATP synthase peripheral stalk subunit OSCP) predicted to have proton-transporting ATP synthase activity.
source: To investigate if energy production is critical for enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 mutant animals, we performed neuron-specific RNAi knockdown of atp-3, an ortholog of human ATP5PO (ATP synthase peripheral stalk subunit OSCP) predicted to have proton-transporting ATP synthase activity.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gene orthology and predicted function.

claim: atp-3 knockdown abrogated the ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration but had no effect on regeneration in WT.
source: atp-3 knockdown abrogated the ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration but had no effect on regeneration in WT (Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: ATP levels were significantly lower in ogt-1 than WT worms.
source: Employing a FRET-based transgenic fluorescence ATP sensor (as described earlier in Soto et al., 2020; Figure 1F, Figure 1—source data 1) as well as ATP measurements in whole worm lysate, we found that ATP levels were significantly lower in ogt-1 than WT worms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from ATP measurements shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There is no measurable difference in pyrophosphate (PPi) levels between WT and ogt-1 worms.
source: In addition, we assessed the ATP utilization from whole animals by measuring the pyrophosphate (PPi) levels as an indirect indication of ATP utilization but found no measurable difference between WT and ogt-1 worms (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from PPi measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Metabolic flux modulation through the majority of the glycolytic pathway and neuron-specific ATP production is important for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration.
source: Taken as a whole, these results infer that metabolic flux modulation through the majority of the glycolytic pathway and neuron-specific ATP production is important for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration, but a complex interaction of metabolic pathways beyond that of canonical glycolysis may be involved specifically within the damaged and regenerating neurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined experimental results presented in the section.

claim: A complex interaction of metabolic pathways beyond that of canonical glycolysis may be involved specifically within the damaged and regenerating neurons in ogt-1 animals.
source: Taken as a whole, these results infer that metabolic flux modulation through the majority of the glycolytic pathway and neuron-specific ATP production is important for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration, but a complex interaction of metabolic pathways beyond that of canonical glycolysis may be involved specifically within the damaged and regenerating neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative claim inferred from the experimental results.

claim: RNA-seq analysis from whole animals identified a substantial number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in ogt-1 compared to WT.
source: We first executed RNA-seq analysis from RNA isolated from whole animals and identified a substantial number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in ogt-1 compared to WT (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway classification analysis of DEGs identified metabolic processes such as carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, and nucleotide metabolism as the most enriched biological processes in ogt-1.
source: Gene ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway classification analysis of DEGs identified metabolic processes such as carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, and nucleotide metabolism as the most enriched biological processes (Figure 2B–C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO and KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Cell membrane, cargo transport, nutrient reservoir, and energy metabolism are enriched in ogt-1.
source: In addition, cell membrane, cargo transport, nutrient reservoir, and energy metabolism are also enriched in ogt-1 (Figure 2B–C, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO and KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: KEGG metabolic pathway enrichment analysis revealed the enrichment of xenobiotics, drug metabolism along with glutathione metabolism, energy metabolism, amino acid, and nitrogen metabolic pathways in ogt-1.
source: KEGG metabolic pathway enrichment analysis revealed the enrichment of xenobiotics, drug metabolism along with glutathione metabolism, energy metabolism, amino acid, and nitrogen metabolic pathways (Figure 2D, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GO molecular function analysis highlights the nutrient reservoir, glutathione, and s-adenosyl methionine (SAM) dependent molecular functions in ogt-1.
source: GO molecular function analysis highlights the nutrient reservoir, glutathione, and s-adenosyl methionine (SAM) dependent molecular functions (Figure 2E, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO molecular function analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The enrichment of amino acid, nucleotide, glutathione, and SAM-dependent metabolic pathways indicate a possible role of OCM and its offshoot pathways in ogt-1 mutant mediated regeneration.
source: The enrichment of amino acid, nucleotide, glutathione, and SAM-dependent metabolic pathways indicate a possible role of OCM and its offshoot pathways in ogt-1 mutant mediated regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the RNA-seq pathway analysis results.

claim: Neuron-specific RNA-seq analysis identified a significant number of DEGs between WT and ogt-1 worms.
source: Neuron-specific RNA-seq analysis identified a significant number of DEGs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by neuron-specific RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Genes linked to HBP and glycolysis such as gaft-1/gfat-2 and pyk-1 were differentially regulated in neuron-specific RNA-seq data.
source: Interestingly, we did find that genes linked to HBP and glycolysis such as gaft-1/gfat-2 and pyk-1 were differentially regulated in our neuron-specific RNA-seq data (Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by neuron-specific RNA-seq data.

claim: GO pathway analysis of neuron-specific DEGs identified metabolic processes such as cellular, macromolecule, nitrogen compound, nucleic acid metabolism in ogt-1.
source: As with whole worm analysis, GO pathway analysis of neuron-specific DEGs identified metabolic processes such as cellular, macromolecule, nitrogen compound, nucleic acid metabolism, etc. (Figure 2F, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO pathway analysis of neuron-specific RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: GO analysis of twofold up-regulated genes revealed neuron-specific pathways (neuronal perception, chemical and olfactory perception, synapses, etc.) along with carbohydrate and polysaccharide metabolic pathways in ogt-1.
source: GO analysis of twofold up-regulated genes revealed neuron-specific pathways as anticipated (neuronal perception, chemical and olfactory perception, synapses, etc.) along with carbohydrate and polysaccharide metabolic pathways (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, Figure 2—source data 2)
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Twofold down-regulated genes included biological processes like meiosis, mitosis, gamete/germ cell production and maturation, reproduction, cell cycle, nuclear division, and embryonic developments in ogt-1.
source: while twofold down-regulated genes included biological processes like meiosis, mitosis, gamete/germ cell production and maturation, reproduction, cell cycle, nuclear division, and embryonic developments, etc. which are expected to be down regulated in the neuronal tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Top 50 up and down-regulated genes include important genes regulated by daf-2 and daf-16 which have been reported to play a critical role in adult neuron function and regeneration.
source: Our top 50 up and down-regulated genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) include important genes regulated by daf-2 and daf-16 which have been reported to play a critical role in adult neuron function and regeneration (Kaletsky et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data and citation to Kaletsky et al., 2016.

claim: folr-1, metr-1, sams-1, important genes for OCM, were significantly up-regulated in the ogt-1 background compared to WT.
source: Employing whole animal qRT-PCR, we further confirmed that folr-1, metr-1, sams-1, important genes for OCM, were significantly up-regulated in the ogt-1 background compared to WT (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: DNA methyltransferase (damt-1) was significantly down regulated in ogt-1.
source: While DNA methyltransferase (damt-1) was significantly down regulated and DNA demethylases (nmad-1) was unchanged (Figure 2G)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: DNA demethylases (nmad-1) was unchanged in ogt-1.
source: While DNA methyltransferase (damt-1) was significantly down regulated and DNA demethylases (nmad-1) was unchanged (Figure 2G)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Bioinformatic analysis of neuron-specific DEGs revealed the enrichment of metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, lipid metabolism along with SSP, OCM, amino acid, nucleotide, and nitrogen compound metabolism in ogt-1.
source: Further bioinformatic analysis of neuron-specific DEGs using the Functional Annotation Tool 'DAVID Bioinformatics Resources' revealed the enrichment of metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, lipid metabolism along with SSP, OCM, amino acid, nucleotide, and nitrogen compound metabolism, etc. (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by DAVID bioinformatics analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Biosynthesis of cofactor analysis specified enrichment of Folate, Methionine, and SAM metabolism cycles, glutathione metabolism, and ATP synthesis pathways in ogt-1.
source: While biosynthesis of cofactor analysis specified enrichment of Folate, Methionine, and SAM metabolism cycles, glutathione metabolism, and ATP synthesis pathways (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by biosynthesis of cofactor analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: NCT502 is a chemical agent reported to inhibit the mammalian phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) enzyme, which catalyzes the first and rate-limiting step of serine biosynthesis.
source: NCT502 (MCE HY-117240) is a chemical agent reported to inhibits the mammalian phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) enzyme, which catalyzes the first and rate-limiting step of serine biosynthesis (Tabatabaie et al., 2010; Zogg, 2014; Pacold et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles describing NCT502.

claim: NCT502 abrogated the effect of ogt-1 mutation on neuronal regeneration but significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms.
source: Applied to C. elegans, NCT502 abrogated the effect of ogt-1 mutation on neuronal regeneration but significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3B, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from NCT502 treatment shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The supplementation of L-serine rescued the abrogative effect of NCT502 in ogt-1.
source: In addition, we observe that the supplementation of L-serine, the final product of SSP, which feeds into OCM, rescued the abrogative effect of NCT502 in ogt-1 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from L-serine supplementation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: akt-1 mutation blocked the enhanced regeneration of ogt-1.
source: Previously we found that AKT kinase, akt-1, activity, plays an important role in ogt-1 regeneration, akt-1 mutation blocked the enhanced regeneration of ogt-1, while gain of function akt-1(++) phenocopied ogt-1 effect (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: Gain of function akt-1(++) phenocopied ogt-1 effect on regeneration.
source: Previously we found that AKT kinase, akt-1, activity, plays an important role in ogt-1 regeneration, akt-1 mutation blocked the enhanced regeneration of ogt-1, while gain of function akt-1(++) phenocopied ogt-1 effect (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: NCT502 blocked the enhanced regeneration in ogt-1(-); akt-1(++) worms.
source: Interestingly, NCT502 blocked the enhanced regeneration in ogt-1(-); akt-1(++) worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Serine supplementation rescued the enhanced regeneration that is eliminated in akt-1(-);ogt-1(-) worms.
source: and serine supplementation rescued the enhanced regeneration that is eliminated in akt-1(-);ogt-1(-) worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against C31C9.2 (termed as phgdh-1), the C. elegans ortholog of human PHGDH, abrogated the effects of ogt-1-mediated regeneration.
source: In concordance with NCT502 treatment, neuron-specific RNAi against C31C9.2 (termed as phgdh-1), the C. elegans ortholog of human PHGDH and target of NCT502, abrogated the effects of ogt-1-mediated regeneration, and significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms even beyond that of ogt-1 worms (Figure 3C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against C31C9.2 (phgdh-1) significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms even beyond that of ogt-1 worms.
source: In concordance with NCT502 treatment, neuron-specific RNAi against C31C9.2 (termed as phgdh-1), the C. elegans ortholog of human PHGDH and target of NCT502, abrogated the effects of ogt-1-mediated regeneration, and significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms even beyond that of ogt-1 worms (Figure 3C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Systemic RNAi knockdown against C31C9.2 (phgdh-1), that is ineffective in neurons, did not alter regeneration levels in ogt-1 animals.
source: Interestingly, systemic RNAi knockdown against C31C9.2 (phgdh-1), that is ineffective in neurons, did not alter regeneration levels in ogt-1 animals suggesting a neuron-specific mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from systemic RNAi knockdown.

claim: Systemic RNAi knockdown against C31C9.2 (phgdh-1) significantly increased regeneration in WT worms.
source: However, it did significantly increase regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: pyk-1 activity was significantly enhanced by NCT502 treatment in WT worms.
source: We further measured pyk-1 activity in WT worms and found that it was significantly enhanced by NCT502 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) suggesting increased glycolytic activity upon blocking the SSP.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pyk-1 activity assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: NCT502 treatment suggests increased glycolytic activity upon blocking the SSP.
source: We further measured pyk-1 activity in WT worms and found that it was significantly enhanced by NCT502 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) suggesting increased glycolytic activity upon blocking the SSP.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the pyk-1 activity data.

claim: pyk-1 activity was equally enhanced in ogt-1 worms with NCT502 treatment.
source: Interestingly, we observed equally enhanced pyk-1 activity in ogt-1 worms with NCT502 treatment (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pyk-1 activity assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The SSP pathway is important in ogt-1-mediated enhanced neuron regeneration.
source: These results demonstrate the importance of the SSP pathway in ogt-1-mediated enhanced neuron regeneration but suggest that in wild-type animals the reverse may be true and blocking SSP becomes beneficial.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results on SSP.

claim: In wild-type animals blocking SSP becomes beneficial for regeneration.
source: These results demonstrate the importance of the SSP pathway in ogt-1-mediated enhanced neuron regeneration but suggest that in wild-type animals the reverse may be true and blocking SSP becomes beneficial.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results showing increased WT regeneration with SSP blockade.

claim: metr-1 is an ortholog of the human MTR gene.
source: To test the importance of OCM in ogt-1-mediated regeneration directly, we tested mutations of methionine synthase (metr-1), an ortholog of the human MTR gene and s-adenosyl methionine synthetase-1 (sams-1), an ortholog of human MAT1A and MAT2A genes, in the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;metr-1, and ogt-1;sams-1) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gene orthology.

claim: sams-1 is an ortholog of human MAT1A and MAT2A genes.
source: To test the importance of OCM in ogt-1-mediated regeneration directly, we tested mutations of methionine synthase (metr-1), an ortholog of the human MTR gene and s-adenosyl methionine synthetase-1 (sams-1), an ortholog of human MAT1A and MAT2A genes, in the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;metr-1, and ogt-1;sams-1) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gene orthology.

claim: Both metr-1 and sams-1 mutations abrogated the enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals but had no significant effect on WT regeneration.
source: Both mutations abrogated the enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals but had no significant effect on WT regeneration (Figure 3E, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic mutations shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Methionine supplementation increases OCM flux.
source: Methionine is an important metabolite of the OCM cycle and its supplementation increases OCM flux (Miousse et al., 2017; Sanderson et al., 2019; Ligthart-Melis et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: Methionine supplementation significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms but had no additional effect on ogt-1 worms.
source: Methionine supplementation significantly increased the regeneration in WT worms but had no additional effect on ogt-1 worms (Figure 3F, Figure 3—source data 1, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from methionine supplementation shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Methionine supplementation did not alter the effects of blocking the SSP in either WT or ogt-1 animals.
source: Nor did it alter the effects of blocking the SSP in either WT or ogt-1 animals (Figure 3F, Figure 3—source data 1) which may be in part due to the requirement of serine for normal OCM progression downstream (Yang and Vousden, 2016; Clare et al., 2019; Geeraerts et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F and citations explaining the mechanism.

claim: SAM mediates numerous cellular processes including several biosynthetic, post-translational modifications and epigenetic modifications of histones and nucleic acids for regulation of gene expression and metabolism, including glycolysis.
source: SAM, a product of SAMS-1 and an important metabolite of OCM, mediates numerous cellular processes including several biosynthetic, post-translational modifications and epigenetic modifications of histones and nucleic acids for regulation of gene expression and metabolism, including glycolysis (Ducker and Rabinowitz, 2017; Clare et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles describing SAM functions.

claim: SAM participates in the Kennedy pathway to synthesize lipid (Phosphatidyl Choline) an important component of the cellular membrane.
source: It participates in the Kennedy pathway to synthesize lipid (Phosphatidyl Choline) an important component of the cellular membrane (Figure 3G; Walker, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Walker, 2017 and illustrated in Figure 3G.

claim: Choline supplementation in ogt-1;sams-1 dual mutant failed to rescue the effects of sams-1 mutation.
source: However, we found that choline supplementation in ogt-1;sams-1 dual mutant failed to rescue the effects of sams-1 mutation (Figure 3H, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from choline supplementation shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against phosphoethanolamine methyl transferase (pmt-1), involved in phosphatidyl choline biosynthesis from SAM, did not reduce ogt-1-mediated regeneration.
source: Furthermore, neuron-specific RNAi against phosphoethanolamine methyl transferase (pmt-1), involved in phosphatidyl choline biosynthesis from SAM, did not reduce ogt-1-mediated regeneration, although it did enhance the regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3H, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against pmt-1 enhanced the regeneration in WT worms.
source: Furthermore, neuron-specific RNAi against phosphoethanolamine methyl transferase (pmt-1), involved in phosphatidyl choline biosynthesis from SAM, did not reduce ogt-1-mediated regeneration, although it did enhance the regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3H, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Knocking down H3K4 methyltransferases (set-2, set-11, set-16, and set-17) had no significant effect on ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration.
source: Knocking down these methyltransferases had no significant effect on ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration but significantly increased regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3I, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Knocking down H3K4 methyltransferases (set-2, set-11, set-16, and set-17) significantly increased regeneration in WT worms.
source: Knocking down these methyltransferases had no significant effect on ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration but significantly increased regeneration in WT worms (Figure 3I, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 3I.

claim: RNA-seq analysis showed that DNA methylases (damt-1) and demethylase (nmad-1) as well as pmt-1/pmt-2, required for Phosphatidyl Choline synthesis from SAM, were all relatively downregulated while OCM genes were relatively upregulated in neuronal tissue in ogt-1 animals.
source: RNA-seq analysis also showed that DNA methylases (damt-1) and demethylase (nmad-1) as well as pmt-1/pmt-2, required for Phosphatidyl Choline synthesis from SAM, were all relatively downregulated while OCM genes were relatively upregulated in neuronal tissue in ogt-1 animals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The functional OCM pathway mediated by MERT-1 and SAMS-1 is essential for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration.
source: Thus, while the functional OCM pathway mediated by MERT-1 and SAMS-1 is essential for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration, these results suggest that it does not act through either lipogenesis or transmethylation pathways involved in epigenetic regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results on OCM.

claim: The functional OCM pathway does not act through either lipogenesis or transmethylation pathways involved in epigenetic regulation in ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration.
source: Thus, while the functional OCM pathway mediated by MERT-1 and SAMS-1 is essential for ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration, these results suggest that it does not act through either lipogenesis or transmethylation pathways involved in epigenetic regulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental results.

claim: The transsulfuration pathway involves cysteine and cystathionine metabolism that is utilized in glutathione synthesis important for oxidative stress maintenance in neurons.
source: The transsulfuration pathway involves cysteine and cystathionine metabolism that is utilized in glutathione synthesis important for oxidative stress maintenance in neurons (Vitvitsky et al., 2006; Sbodio et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles describing the transsulfuration pathway.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against glutathione synthetase (gss-1) detected no effect on the enhanced regeneration in the ogt-1 mutant background but significantly increased regeneration in WT.
source: Performing neuron-specific RNAi against glutathione synthetase (gss-1), an ortholog of GSS, we detected no effect on the enhanced regeneration in the ogt-1 mutant background but significantly increased regeneration in WT (Figure 4B, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Supplementation with L-Glutathione (GHS) significantly decreased regeneration in ogt-1 worms but had no effect on WT worms.
source: In a complimentary manor, supplementation with L-Glutathione (GHS) significantly decreased regeneration in ogt-1 worms but had no effect on WT worms (Figure 4B, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from glutathione supplementation shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Supplementation with L-cystathionine had no detectable effect on regeneration in ogt-1 worms or WT.
source: By contrast, supplementation with L-cystathionine had no detectable effect on regeneration in ogt-1 worms or WT (Figure 4C, Figure 4—source data 1)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cystathionine supplementation shown in Figure 4C.

claim: L-cystathionine supplementation rescued the effect of blocking SSP with NCT502 in ogt-1 worms.
source: but rescued the effect of blocking SSP with NCT502 in ogt-1 worms (Figure 4C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The transsulfuration pathway is functionally involved in ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration but not through glutathione synthesis.
source: These observations suggest that while the transsulfuration pathway is functionally involved in ogt-1-mediated enhanced regeneration it is not through glutathione synthesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results on the transsulfuration pathway.

claim: Cystathionine can be metabolized into succinyl-CoA or acetyl-CoA through either the vitamin B12 dependent canonical pathway or the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathways, respectively.
source: Cystathionine can be further metabolized into succinyl-CoA or acetyl-CoA through either the vitamin B12 dependent canonical pathway or the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathways, respectively (Watson et al., 2016; Giese et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles describing cystathionine metabolism.

claim: Neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in OCM (metr-1, sams-1, folr-1, mthf-1, etc.) were relatively upregulated in ogt-1 animals.
source: Our neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in OCM (metr-1, sams-1, folr-1, mthf-1, etc.) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), transsulfuration (cth-1) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and the downstream vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway (acdh-1, ech-6, hach-1, hphd-1, and alh-8) were relatively upregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) in ogt-1 animals
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in transsulfuration (cth-1) were relatively upregulated in ogt-1 animals.
source: Our neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in OCM (metr-1, sams-1, folr-1, mthf-1, etc.) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), transsulfuration (cth-1) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and the downstream vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway (acdh-1, ech-6, hach-1, hphd-1, and alh-8) were relatively upregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) in ogt-1 animals
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in the downstream vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway (acdh-1, ech-6, hach-1, hphd-1, and alh-8) were relatively upregulated in ogt-1 animals.
source: Our neuronal cell-specific RNA-seq analysis revealed that genes involved in OCM (metr-1, sams-1, folr-1, mthf-1, etc.) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), transsulfuration (cth-1) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and the downstream vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway (acdh-1, ech-6, hach-1, hphd-1, and alh-8) were relatively upregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) in ogt-1 animals
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Genes involved in the vitamin B12 dependent canonical pathway (pcca-1, pccb-1, mce-1, and mmcm-1) were down regulated in ogt-1 animals.
source: while genes involved in the vitamin B12 dependent canonical pathway (pcca-1, pccb-1, mce-1, and mmcm-1) were down regulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis showed that genes involved in TSP (cth-1, cht-2) and in the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway showed unidirectional upregulated expression in ogt-1.
source: Likewise, performing qRT-PCR analysis against genes in these pathways, we found that genes involved in TSP (cth-1, cht-2) and in the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway showed unidirectional upregulated expression in ogt-1 (Figure 4D)
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis showed that genes involved in the canonical vitamin B12 dependent pathway showed no clear trend in differential expression in ogt-1.
source: while genes involved in the canonical vitamin B12 dependent pathway showed no clear trend in differential expression (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The mce-1 mutation had no effect on regeneration in either WT or the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;mce-1).
source: The mce-1 mutation had no effect on regeneration in either WT or the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;mce-1) (Figure 4F, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic mutations shown in Figure 4F.

claim: acdh-1 mutation had no effect on WT regeneration but selectively eliminated the enhanced regeneration of the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;cdh-1).
source: However, while acdh-1 mutation had no effect on WT regeneration, it selectively eliminated the enhanced regeneration of the ogt-1 background (ogt-1;cdh-1) (Figure 4F, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic mutations shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against acdh-1 and mce-1 in the ogt-1 background recapitulated the results from genetic mutations.
source: These results were recapitulated using neuron-specific RNAi knockdown against acdh-1 and mce-1 in the ogt-1 background (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against mce-1 in the ogt-1;acdh-1 double mutant had no observable effect.
source: Neuron-specific RNAi against mce-1 in the ogt-1;acdh-1 double mutant had no observable effect (Figure 4F, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against pod-2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase), important for lipid synthesis from acetyl CoA, had no effect on either WT or ogt-1 regeneration.
source: Thus, we tested if lipid synthesis plays a role by neuron-specific RNAi against pod-2 (acetyl-CoA carboxylase), an ortholog of human ACACA (acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha), that is important for lipid synthesis from acetyl CoA, but found it had no effect on either WT or ogt-1 regeneration (Figure 4G, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 worms was blocked by neuron-specific RNAi against atp-3 RNAi that reduces cellular ATP production.
source: In contrast, the enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 worms was clearly blocked by neuron-specific RNAi against atp-3 RNAi that reduces cellular ATP production, (as described above earlier Figure 1C and Figure 4G, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Perturbation in O-GlcNAc signaling is known to affect lipid metabolism.
source: Since perturbation in O-GlcNAc signaling is known to affect lipid metabolism (Lockridge and Hanover, 2022) and lipid metabolism is a significant source of energy in neurons (Tracey et al., 2018), we investigated if ATP generation via beta-oxidation of lipids plays a role.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lockridge and Hanover, 2022.

claim: Lipid metabolism is a significant source of energy in neurons.
source: Since perturbation in O-GlcNAc signaling is known to affect lipid metabolism (Lockridge and Hanover, 2022) and lipid metabolism is a significant source of energy in neurons (Tracey et al., 2018), we investigated if ATP generation via beta-oxidation of lipids plays a role.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Tracey et al., 2018.

claim: Neuron-specific RNAi against acs-2 or cpt-2 did not affect enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals.
source: However, neuron-specific RNAi against, acs-2, acyl-CoA synthetase family member 2 (ortholog of human ACSF2), or cpt-2, carnitine palmitoyl transferase (ortholog of human CPT1A, carnitine palmitoyl transferase 1 A and CPT1C, carnitine palmitoyl transferase 1 C) did not affect enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from RNAi knockdown shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Both acs-2 and cpt-2 are important for lipid beta-oxidation.
source: While RNAi knockdown does suffer from gene specific variability, both acs-2 and cpt-2 are important for lipid beta-oxidation, suggesting that the process is not fundamental in ogt-1 regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the function of these genes.

claim: Lipid beta-oxidation is not fundamental in ogt-1 regeneration.
source: While RNAi knockdown does suffer from gene specific variability, both acs-2 and cpt-2 are important for lipid beta-oxidation, suggesting that the process is not fundamental in ogt-1 regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNAi knockdown results.

claim: The specific metabolic pathway involves acetyl CoA production by cystathionine metabolism through the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway in ogt-1 regeneration.
source: Regardless, in combination with gene expression analysis, these results help to further define the pathway of ogt-1 regeneration to specifically involve acetyl CoA production by cystathionine metabolism through the vitamin B12 independent shunt pathway.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental and gene expression results.

claim: To initiate and sustain the energetically demanding growth state required for effective regeneration there must be sufficient modulation of the underlying molecular and metabolic processes within the damaged neuron.
source: In order to initiate and sustain the energetically demanding growth state required for effective regeneration there must be sufficient modulation of the underlying molecular and metabolic processes within the damaged neuron (He and Jin, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to He and Jin, 2016.

claim: Glycolysis is a key energy source for neurons, particularly under energy-limiting conditions.
source: Glycolysis is a key energy source for neurons, particularly under energy-limiting conditions (Jang et al., 2016) and in developing neurons that foster high axonal growth rates (Han et al., 2016; Zheng et al., 2016; Han et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: Glycolysis is a key energy source in developing neurons that foster high axonal growth rates.
source: Glycolysis is a key energy source for neurons, particularly under energy-limiting conditions (Jang et al., 2016) and in developing neurons that foster high axonal growth rates (Han et al., 2016; Zheng et al., 2016; Han et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: High O-GlcNAcylation decreases pfk-1.1 function.
source: This is in accordance with the reported effects of O-GlcNAcylation on these enzymes. High O-GlcNAcylation decreases pfk-1.1 function (Bacigalupa et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bacigalupa et al., 2018.

claim: High O-GlcNAcylation destabilizes the pyruvate kinase, PKM1/2, complex.
source: Despite the fact that high O-GlcNAcylation also destabilizes the pyruvate kinase, PKM1/2, complex (Wang et al., 2017), reports show that inhibition of ogt-1 results in low pyruvate kinase expression and cellular activity (Yu et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: Inhibition of ogt-1 results in low pyruvate kinase expression and cellular activity.
source: Despite the fact that high O-GlcNAcylation also destabilizes the pyruvate kinase, PKM1/2, complex (Wang et al., 2017), reports show that inhibition of ogt-1 results in low pyruvate kinase expression and cellular activity (Yu et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2019a.

claim: The ogt-1 mutation, which reduces O-GlcNAcylation, is expected to increase pfk-1.1, and reduce pyk-1, activity.
source: The ogt-1 mutation, which reduces O-GlcNAcylation, is therefore expected to increase pfk-1.1, and reduce pyk-1, activity, respectively, which agrees with their measured importance in ogt-1 neuron regeneration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the known effects of O-GlcNAcylation on these enzymes.

claim: Enhanced glycolysis drives OCM through the SSP.
source: Enhanced glycolysis drives OCM through the SSP (Locasale, 2013; Yu et al., 2019b) that is known to be involved in several neuronal conditions including, neuronal growth, neural tube defect, and Alzheimer's disease (Coppede, 2010; Bonvento and Bolaños, 2021; Lionaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: The SSP is known to be involved in several neuronal conditions including, neuronal growth, neural tube defect, and Alzheimer's disease.
source: Enhanced glycolysis drives OCM through the SSP (Locasale, 2013; Yu et al., 2019b) that is known to be involved in several neuronal conditions including, neuronal growth, neural tube defect, and Alzheimer's disease (Coppede, 2010; Bonvento and Bolaños, 2021; Lionaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: Metabolic flux diverted from the early steps of glycolysis towards OCM through SSP is crucial for enhanced regeneration in ogt-1 mutants.
source: We found that metabolic flux diverted from the early steps of glycolysis towards OCM through SSP is crucial, which is in agreement with earlier reports where enhanced glycolysis diverts metabolic flux towards OCM through SSP (Yu et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results and supported by citation.

claim: Enhanced glycolysis diverts metabolic flux towards OCM through SSP.
source: We found that metabolic flux diverted from the early steps of glycolysis towards OCM through SSP is crucial, which is in agreement with earlier reports where enhanced glycolysis diverts metabolic flux towards OCM through SSP (Yu et al., 2019b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Yu et al., 2019b.

claim: Enhanced glycolysis and/or knock down of PMK1/2 (mammalian ortholog of pyk-1) diverts metabolic flux toward serine synthesis pathway to sustain cellular metabolic requirements.
source: These results are in agreement with earlier metabolomic findings that enhanced glycolysis (Yu et al., 2019b) and/or knock down of PMK1/2 (mammalian ortholog of pyk-1) diverts metabolic flux toward serine synthesis pathway to sustain cellular metabolic requirements (Yu et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: OCM is involved in both lipogenesis and DNA transmethylation.
source: Although OCM is involved in both lipogenesis and DNA transmethylation (Kersten, 2001; Yu et al., 2019b) that could potentially play significant roles in increasing neuron regeneration (Iskandar et al., 2010), we found that the regeneration effects of ogt-1 were primarily dependent on L-cystathionine metabolism via the downstream TSP (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: The TSP is influenced by OCM and its metabolites and has been reported to play an important role in neurodegenerative diseases and ATP production.
source: The TSP is influenced by OCM and its metabolites and has been reported to play an important role in neurodegenerative diseases and ATP production (Giese et al., 2020; Lam et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: The down regulation of pyk-1 from ogt-1 inhibition has been associated with total reduced ATP levels.
source: Indeed, the down regulation of pyk-1 from ogt-1 inhibition has been associated with total reduced ATP levels previously (Dey et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dey et al., 2019.

claim: The HBS pathway nominally shunts off ~5% of glycolytic flux.
source: For instance, the HBS pathway nominally shunts off ~5% of glycolytic flux (Marshall et al., 1991; Bond and Hanover, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: Blocking the HBS pathway through RNAi against gfat-1 and gfat-2 appears to divert metabolic flux towards glycolysis and results in enhanced regeneration in WT animals similar to that of ogt-1.
source: We found that blocking the HBS pathway through RNAi against gfat-1 and gfat-2 (Yi et al., 2012; Jóźwiak and Forma, 2014; Kim et al., 2018), appears to divert metabolic flux towards glycolysis and results in enhanced regeneration in WT animals similar to that of ogt-1 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results and supported by citations.

claim: pyk-1 knockdown increases regeneration in WT and is known to divert metabolic flux toward the SSP.
source: Likewise, pyk-1 knockdown increases regeneration in WT and is known to divert metabolic flux toward the SSP (Yu et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation.

claim: Mutation of the O-GlcNAcase, oga-1, which increases O-GlcNAc levels, also increased neuron regeneration in C. elegans, but did so through an independent pathway of enhanced mitochondrial stress response.
source: Likewise, we had previously found that mutation of the O-GlcNAcase, oga-1, which increases O-GlcNAc levels, also increased neuron regeneration in C. elegans, but did so through an independent pathway of enhanced mitochondrial stress response (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: Glucose supplementation in wild-type animals increases regeneration.
source: For example, we previously demonstrated increased regeneration in wild-type animals with glucose supplementation (Taub et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation.

claim: L-methionine supplementation or treatment with the SSP blocking agent NCT502 increases regeneration in wild-type animals.
source: Here, we find similar effects with L-methionine supplementation or treatment with the SSP blocking agent NCT502 in wild-type animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nutrient supplements and metabolic drug targets have been employed in neurotherapeutic treatments and prevention in numerous contexts including neuronal developmental defects and age-associated neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Nutrient supplements and metabolic drug targets have been employed in neurotherapeutic treatments and prevention in numerous contexts including neuronal developmental defects (Greene et al., 2017; Businaro et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2022) and age-associated neurodegenerative diseases (Stempler et al., 2014; Businaro et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: O-GlcNAc signaling has been widely implicated in regulating various neuronal cellular processes in higher organisms including axon growth, synaptic plasticity, and neurite outgrowth.
source: While our current study has specifically focused on the neuronal regeneration of the mechanosensory neurons in C. elegans, O-GlcNAc signaling has been widely implicated in regulating various neuronal cellular processes in higher organisms. This includes axon growth, synaptic plasticity, and neurite outgrowth (Tian et al., 2023; Mutalik and Gupton, 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: O-GlcNAc signaling has been linked to the modulation of gene expression during neuronal repair in higher animals including mammals.
source: and has been linked to the modulation of gene expression during neuronal repair in higher animals including mammals (Lee et al., 2021; Su and Schwarz, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to research articles.

claim: Functions of O-GlcNAc signaling are conserved throughout the nervous system and across species.
source: These studies suggest that functions of O-GlcNAc signaling are conserved throughout the nervous system and across species.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on O-GlcNAc signaling.
